tab_description: Upload your watermark signature to authorize high-risk work — typically when calling API models: creating red/blue-team drill or penetration-testing agents and skills, or performing dangerous task behavior. Each upload generates a dedicated Ed25519 keypair; the private key never leaves this machine.
enable_purpose: Signature authorization lets you explicitly authorize high-risk work in Multica tasks after uploading your watermark signature — typically while calling API models: creating red-team / blue-team drill or penetration-testing agents and skills, or performing dangerous task behavior.
enable_point_offensive: Authorizes agents to run attack tests or penetration tests within the environment and against the targets you specify
enable_point_agents: Authorizes the creation of dangerous agents, agent teams, or skills dedicated to such work
enable_point_tasks: Attaches a cryptographically verifiable authorization declaration to every covered run — the model knows it is authorized, and the risk is yours
enable_risk: You acknowledge that misdirected operations can cause real damage, that Multica's server-side scope enforcement constrains what agents can do but cannot judge intent, and that you assume full responsibility for every authorization you sign.
enable_ack: I have read the purpose above, understand and accept the risks, and want to enable signature authorization for this workspace.
enable_off_note: Disabled by default. While off, no watermark can be uploaded, nothing can be signed, no attestation reaches agent runs, and verification is refused — even for records that already exist.
enable_armed_note: Signature authorization is enabled. Disabling immediately suspends signing, verification, and attestation injection (existing records are kept).
asset_empty: No signature asset yet. Upload a watermark image (PNG with transparency works best) to enable signing.
asset_retire_confirm: Retire this signature? Existing authorizations stay verifiable; new signings must upload a new watermark.
history_revoke_confirm: Revoke this authorization? Covered tasks stop receiving the attestation on their next run.
ceremony_scope: This signature covers this issue and all its subsequent runs. Editing the task invalidates the authorization until re-signed.
ceremony_signed: Authorized — declaration injected into the runtime
ceremony_no_asset: No signature on this machine yet
ceremony_no_asset_hint: Upload your watermark signature in Settings → Signatures first.
ceremony_responsibility: By signing I confirm this task involves high-risk operations, acknowledge the risks, and assume full responsibility. This authorization covers only the scope above.
